newsitem.title: GERMANY: Metalbank says took on Kolbenschmidt stake.
newsitem.headline: Metalbank says took on Kolbenschmidt stake.

text.p: Metallbank GmbH, the banking unit once part of Metallgesellschaft AG, confirmed on Tuesday it had taken over a 24.99 percent stake in the car components group Kolbenschmidt AG.
The company said it had already passed the stake, which was formerly held by Commerzbank AG, onward at a discount of around five percent to the market value.
It also said that the British engineering firm T&N had an option on the package.

T&N Plc had an option to buy Commerzbank's former 49.99 percent holding in Kolbenschmidt but was blocked from doing so by German cartel authorities. That option was due to expire at the end of this year and Commerzbank said it had no plans to extend it.

Separately, T&N said it had extended its option on a 24.99 percent stake in Kolbenschmidt until September 1997 and that Commerzbank had passed the stake on to Metallbank, which was acting for a group of European investors.
It said an announcement about its option for the further 24.99 percent in the group would be made shortly.

Metallbank trading division manager Lothar Mark told Reuters in a telephone interview that the transaction with 6.7 million Kolbenschmidt shares had cost some 125 million marks -- around five percent below the market value of the shares.
Sources in Munich had named Metallbank as the taker for the package, which Commerzbank said it had passed onward.
Kolbenschmidt shares closed bourse trade on Tuesday 21 pfennigs lower at 19.30 marks, broadly in line with the market trend.
In post-bourse electronic dealings, the shares were still at 19.30 marks, up 60 pfennigs from their close in late dealings Monday.
